change.title: ao-replay/9055-r5
change.description: refactor(chat): keep attaching during a restore to the case that needs it
change.author: Dhruv Sharma

findings.title: Staging POST no longer receives the abort signal
findings.body: The diff removes `signal,` from the `POST /api/v1/sessions/{sessionId}/attachments` call. The `signal` that `ChatComposer.prepareAttachments` passes (ChatComposer.tsx:753) is aborted when the user removes a pending file (useFileAttachments.ts:652, `whenAllAborted` at 568). It now reaches only `toWireAttachments`, which uses it for large-file uploads (attachment-uploads.ts:42). A small inline file's staging request is no longer cancelled by removal. The request still runs, and a slow or stalled one keeps the hook busy. The daemon still writes the removed file into the session worktree. The wait on `restore.continue()` at line 2428 ignores the signal as well, so removing a pending file during a restore does not stop it either. The useFileAttachments tests at lines 441-485 rely on the signal reaching the preparer. Pass `signal` to the POST and race the restore wait against it.

findings.title: Removing the guard shows a false "Nothing was attached" error after the user cancels every pending file
findings.body: The deleted line `if (acceptedFresh.every((attachment) => cancelled(attachment.id))) return [];` sat in the batch-path catch (non-`prepareEach`, which is what ChatComposer uses without cloud attachments). When the user removes every pending file, `whenAllAborted` aborts the preparer (lines 568-569). If staging rejects because of that abort (a large-file upload does, via attachment-uploads.ts:35-42), the catch now falls through to `errors.add("Files couldn’t be saved. Nothing was attached.")` and `setError`. The user cancelled on purpose and still sees a failure banner. The per-file path at lines 555 and 560 still checks `signal.aborted`, and the batch path no longer does. Restore the guard.

findings.title: Enter on a file-only draft is silently ignored during a send
findings.body: The hold condition during an in-flight submit is now `textRef.current.trim() || fileAttachments.hasPendingReads()`. A file that has already finished staging, with no text, does not count. Enter then reaches `return submitInFlight.current` and nothing is held or sent. The chip stays and the user has to press Enter again after the first send lands. Before this change `nextDraftHasFiles` counted settled staged files too. The new test at ChatComposer.optimistic.test.tsx:152 presses Enter while staging is still pending, so it only covers the pending-read case. Add a test for Enter after the file has settled, and either hold that draft or accept the behaviour on purpose.

findings.title: Files taken for the next message cannot be removed while the first one sends
findings.body: Remove is now disabled by `controlsDisabled || queuedEditRecovery || draftMutationPending || fileAttachments.preparing`. `draftMutationPending` is true for the whole optimistic send (line 955-956), which is when `takesNextFiles` lets the user add files. Files can be added during a restore but not removed until it finishes. The old `attachBlocked` exempted `takesNextFiles`, and a removed test covered removal. A wrong file added while a slow restore runs gets sent with the next message unless the user waits.

findings.title: A held message now picks up files added after its Enter
findings.body: `HeldSubmit.files` and the `nextFilesKey()` check were removed. The held send is now guarded only by `textRef.current !== heldSubmit.text`. A file attached after the user pressed Enter but before the first send lands is added to the held message. The removed test "does not send a held message whose files changed after its Enter" covered this. Is that intended?

findings.title: Is Mutation.continue() safe for waiting on a running restore?
findings.body: `restore.continue()` resumes a paused mutation. If a mutation is `pending` but its retryer does not exist yet (between the pending dispatch and `onMutate` finishing), TanStack's `continue()` falls back to `execute(variables)`. That would start a second restore. The previous `restoreInFlight` map only awaited the existing promise. Have you checked that this window cannot be hit in the installed @tanstack/react-query version? If not, a plain wait on the mutation's settle would be safer.

findings.title: Dropped tests leave the new restore-wait and the remount cases uncovered
findings.body: The deleted tests covered a restore started outside the chat, and the chat being hidden or remounted while a send lands (the `Activity` tests). The new `useStageAttachments` path waits on the `resume-agent` mutation key, and the remaining tests only cover the case where the chat's own `send` starts the restore. There is no test for a restore started by `ResumeAgentControl` or `SessionView` (same mutation key), for `archived=false` not waiting, or for a restore started through `useRestoreSession` directly, which is no longer awaited at all.

contracts.action: Stage attachments wait for a pending restore through the mutation cache instead of the restoreInFlight map
contracts.equivalent_path: Removed `restoreInFlight` in useRestoreSession.ts, which awaited the in-flight restore promise and asserted success
contracts.before_after: Before: any restore through useRestoreSession was awaited, and a failure became SESSION_RESTORE_FAILED. After: only pending `resume-agent` mutations are awaited, and only when `archived` is true, so a restore called directly through useRestoreSession is not awaited. A rejected mutation makes `continue()` reject with the mutation's error, which already carries SESSION_RESTORE_FAILED (useConversation.ts:1252).
contracts.visible_effect: A file pasted during a restore stays in the Attaching state until the restore finishes. If the restore fails, the file attach fails and the composer shows the send error message.
contracts.failure_mode: The abort signal is not honoured while waiting. Whether `continue()` can re-run a restore on a mutation that has no retryer yet was not confirmed.
contracts.open_question: Does Mutation.continue() in the installed @tanstack/query-core re-execute a pending mutation whose retryer is not created yet?

contracts.action: The composer takes files for the next message during a restore only when the sent message had no files
contracts.equivalent_path: Previously `dropSent` and `unsentAttachments` filtered the sent files out of the live list. Now `sentFiles` turns file intake off and the strip hides the list.
contracts.before_after: After the accepted send, `clearAcceptedDraft` and `applyAcceptedDraftResult` clear or reconcile `fileAttachments` against the persisted draft (lines 1175-1183). That is safe because next files are only taken when the sent message had none.
contracts.visible_effect: Files added during a restore appear as chips and are sent with the next Enter. When the sent message had files, Attach is disabled and its chips are hidden.
contracts.failure_mode: Enter on a file-only draft that has already settled is ignored during the send (finding at line 1767). Remove is disabled for next files (finding at line 2693).

contracts.action: Staging POST now sent without the abort signal
contracts.equivalent_path: useFileAttachments aborts per-file controllers on cancelPending, remove and clear, and passes the signal to prepareAttachments
contracts.before_after: Before: the POST was aborted with the signal. After: only toWireAttachments sees it, so the POST runs to completion after the file is removed.
contracts.visible_effect: A removed file can still be written into the worktree. In the batch path a spurious save-failed error can show, because the cancel guard was also deleted (useFileAttachments.ts:577).
contracts.failure_mode: A stalled staging request is not cancellable.

summary: The PR removes the sent-file bookkeeping and has the stager wait on a pending `resume-agent` mutation instead of the `restoreInFlight` map. Two regressions tie the removed code to the abort path. The staging POST no longer gets the abort signal, and the cancelled-batch guard in `useFileAttachments` is gone, so removing every pending file can show a false "Nothing was attached" error. There are also behaviour gaps: Enter on an already-settled file-only draft during a send is ignored, next-message files cannot be removed during a restore, and a held message can pick up files added after its Enter. Whether `Mutation.continue()` is safe on a running mutation is an open question. I deleted tests and did not replace the coverage for the restore wait and the hidden/remounted-chat cases.
